text.p: The Bank of England's new monetary policy committee, which has been empowered by the Labour government to set interest rates, will announce the outcome of its first meeting at 1100 GMT/1200 BST on Friday.
Following are key facts about the meeting:
* The committee reconvened shortly after 0700 GMT/0800 BST on Friday.
* Six members had voting rights at the first meeting:
BANK OF ENGLAND -- Governor Eddie George, deputy governor Howard Davies#, executive directors Mervyn King and Ian Plenderleith.
OUTSIDE MEMBERS -- Charles Goodhart, Professor of Banking and Finance at the London School of Economics, Willem Buiter, Professor of International Macroeconmics at Cambridge University.

* Sir Alan Budd, chief economic adviser to the Treasury, was at the meeting as the non-voting Treasury observer. He will take up his voting position on the committee when he retires from the Treasury later this year.
DeAnne Julius, British Airways Plc chief economist and the last outside appointee, will join the committee in September.
* Any vote on interest rates will be carried on a simple majority with all six members voting. If the vote is tied, the governor will have a second casting vote.
* Minutes of the meeting, including details of any vote taken, will be published by the Bank no later than six weeks after the meeting.
* Members of the committee have been asked not to comment publicly on monetary issues in the week of the meeting and the day after.

* British interest rates were raised on May 6 by a quarter point to 6.25 percent. The Bank said in its quarterly Inflation Report a week later that rates would probably have to rise further to keep inflation down.

# Howard Davies is leaving the Bank of England in August to become head of the Securities and Investments Board. His replacement will be announced by the Treasury soon, possibly this week. A second deputy governor will be appointed once new legislation creating the post has been passed. This is not expected before the summer recess.
